## Historical audit: S0278

**Source:** `/srv/lab-disks/disk2/users/xymo/Documents/Codex/2026-11-02/scene-rsi-rsi-1-3d-blender/outputs/scene_rsi_v3/results/H03/selection/bw_0045/1/trajectory.jsonl`. All citations below refer to this file. The supplied observations include the full indicated JSONL lines; no image pixels were available to this audit.

**Goal versus observation.** The requested goal was a camera-matched, editable 3D reconstruction from one photograph, with numerical anchor diagnostics (H request, line 1). The student’s inventory interpreted the scene as a dairy barn with reclining cows, stall rails, architecture and a worker. That interpretation is not independent verification of the photograph (H response, line 3).

| Stage | Evidence and result |
|---|---|
| Initial build | H emitted separate architecture, six rail-divider groups, nine cows, worker and bedding, with named child parts. Cow parts were positioned as reclining bodies with folded legs; rail segments were grouped into loops. Color families, metallic/roughness settings, world, camera and two lights were specified; straw was geometric rather than an image texture. Hierarchy and named parts do not establish physical connection or visual fidelity (lines 3–4). |
| Failure and repair | Step 1 failed before rendering: the runner rejected an import outside its frozen contract; the program imported `json`, absent from the displayed allowed list. The actual traceback and instruction not to infer visual defects were delivered to H (lines 7–8). H removed that import and formatted the diagnostic table manually; step 2 built and rendered successfully (lines 10–16). This is evidence of adoption of execution feedback, not a teacher intervention. |
| Review and revision | The next H request supplied the reference, step-2 render and a comparison instruction (line 18). H **claimed** the cow was too small and ball-like, the wall cropped, curb slope insufficient and rails too straight; it also said the worker was occluded and the old muzzle anchor mismatched (line 20). These are student diagnoses, not independently inspected image findings. H executed a revision enlarging/moving the foreground cow, changing camera, wall, door, rail loops, colors and lighting (lines 20–21). |
| Validation and outcome | Step 2 printed substantial estimated-anchor residuals, including door-top vertical +0.1991 and rail-bend vertical +0.3496 (line 16, characters [0,61691)). Step 3 tested four camera candidates numerically, selected the lower-lens candidate, built and rendered successfully; residuals still included rail-bend vertical +0.3181 and curb-right horizontal +0.7837 (line 26, characters [0,68668)). These are projections of estimated correspondences, not visibility or image-quality tests. Step 3 was selected (line 27); no subsequent visual review or formal quality score is visible. |

**Teacher and autonomy.** No teacher message, teacher detection, diagnosis, proposed update, or teacher execution appears in this student trajectory; receipt or adoption of teacher advice is unestablished. H independently authored and revised programs and performed numerical camera exploration within the runner, while session logs show no separate tool calls (lines 2, 9, 19–21).

**Assessment and uncertainty.** There was an initial **invalid-program failure**, followed by formal build/render success, not an empty patch or timeout. Overall reconstruction correctness is **unknown**: neither the reference nor final image is visible here, and the selected render was not subsequently assessed in the trace. Multiple objects, materials, pose and intended part relationships are evidenced by code, not verified geometry or appearance. The student’s count estimate for step 3 also describes two loops per divider while its code generates three (line 21). Transferably, traceback-directed repair and separating projection diagnostics from visibility are supported practices; the barn-specific camera, cow and rail corrections remain hypotheses whose visual effectiveness is unresolved.
